title: Whose Hands Held This?
sub: Grades 1–2 · Hands of History · Coins and the people who held them
objective: Children will learn that the coins in the exhibition were really used, two thousand years ago, by people in the land where Jesus lived. They will meet four of those people, match each coin to the hands that held it, and hear how two of the coins belong to stories in the Gospels: the widow who gave everything, and the census that brought Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Every coin here was held by someone, two thousand years ago, in the land where Jesus lived. Their stories reach us through hands just like yours.

items.text: match each coin to the person who held it, using picture clues
items.question: match each coin to the hands that held it?

items.text: tell the story of the widow’s two tiny coins, and why Jesus called her gift the biggest
items.question: tell why the widow’s two tiny coins were the biggest gift?

items.text: say how the emperor’s census brought Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem
items.question: say why Mary and Joseph went to Bethlehem?

items.text: speak or write as one of the people, telling what is in your hands
items.question: be one of the people, and tell their story?

materials: Page 3 of this plan, projected or printed: the four people and their coins
A few coins from a pocket or purse
Four signs for the corners of the room: *Widow, Merchant, Mother, Priest*
Differentiated handouts, one per child; crayons
questions: Look at each person’s hands. What are they doing — giving, counting, holding, working?
Which coin is the smallest? Why do you think the widow’s tiny gift was the biggest to Jesus?
Herod’s coin has no face on it. Whose face is on our coins? Why did Herod leave the face off?
If you could ask one of these people a question, what would you ask?
connection: **Visit the exhibition:** the Widow’s Mite, the Shekel of Tyre and Herod’s coin are all in the cases. Play **Hands of History** together: look at the hands and guess whose they are.
**Virtual visit:** the game, the coins and their stories are all online.

steps.title: Who held this before you?
script: Pass a coin from your pocket around the circle. *“Before this coin came to me, whose hands held it? A shopkeeper? A bus driver? Someone’s grandma?”* Let children guess. Then: *“Some coins are very, very old. Today we will meet people who held coins two thousand years ago, in the land where Jesus lived.”*

steps.title: The Widow
script: **Read the card aloud.** At the Temple, rich people put in large gifts. A poor widow came and put in two tiny coins — all she had. Jesus told his friends she had given more than all the others. Her coin, the lepton, was the smallest coin people used. The exhibition shows **two**, because the Gospel says two.

steps.purpose: Hear the widow’s story: the smallest gift, and the biggest to Jesus.

steps.title: The Merchant
script: **Read the card aloud.** In a busy market, a merchant counts the day’s coins. Many show the face of Augustus Caesar, the emperor in faraway Rome. Augustus ordered a census, a counting of all the people — and that is why Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born.

steps.title: The Mother in Bethlehem
script: **Read the card aloud.** A mother uses small coins to buy bread and oil for her family. King Herod made these coins, and they have no face on them, because Jewish law did not allow it. When Jesus was born, an angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary and the baby to Egypt, where they would be safe.

steps.purpose: Meet an everyday coin with no face, and hear how God kept the Holy Family safe.
students: What will she buy with her coins?
King Herod’s coin has no face. Why not?

steps.title: The Temple Priest
script: **Read the card aloud.** A priest works at the Temple, where people paid a Temple tax each year. The Temple accepted only one coin for it, the shekel of Tyre, because its silver was the purest. The priest held hundreds every day. Ours is a **replica** — a careful copy — because real ones are very rare.

steps.title: Find the hands
script: Put a sign in each corner. Show one coin at a time from page 3 and say its clue (*“the smallest coin of all”*). Children walk to the person who held it. In each corner, invite one or two children to step into the story and speak as that person: *“I am the widow. I am giving my two little coins to God.”*

steps.title: Choose a handout
script: Then children choose a handout. All three levels match the same four coins to the same four people.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Draw a line from each coin to the person who held it, using picture clues. Circle how many coins the widow gave, and draw a gift you could give to God.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: Write the right letter under each coin. Finish four short sentences from a word bank, then say which person you would like to meet, and why.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Match the coins, then choose one person and write two or three sentences as if you were them. Invent the journey of a coin from hand to hand.

steps.purpose: Match the coins on paper, at the right level of challenge.
students: Choose Green, Yellow or Red. All three match the same four coins to the same four people.

steps.title: Look back
script: Ask the objectives back as questions, from the screen or page 1: *“Can you now…?”* For each one, children show a thumb up, sideways or down. Ask one child to answer each aloud; for the last, ask a Red Level child to speak as their person.

steps.title: Closing prayer
script: Ask the children to hold out their open hands. Pray together, a line at a time: *“Jesus, the widow gave you everything in her hands. Here are my hands. Help me to give with a happy heart — my time, my kindness and my love. Amen.”*
